record.original_question: If C_1 and C_2 are two coaxial circles in parallel planes, must every compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface spanning C_1 union C_2 be a surface of revolution?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.7 (4*). Let C1 and C2 be two coaxial circles in parallel planes. Is a compact embedded cmc surface spanning C1 union C2 a surface of revolution?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be two coaxial circles lying in distinct parallel planes of $\mathbb{R}^3$ (i.e., circles whose centers lie on a common line orthogonal to the two parallel planes). Let $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact, connected, embedded smooth surface (with boundary) of constant mean curvature whose boundary is exactly $\partial \Sigma = C_1 \cup C_2$. Must $\Sigma$ be a surface of revolution about the common axis of $C_1$ and $C_2$? Either prove this rotational symmetry holds for every such $\Sigma$, or exhibit a non-rotationally-symmetric example.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in surveys on constant mean curvature surfaces with circular boundary; uniqueness/symmetry of compact embedded CMC surfaces spanning two coaxial circles in parallel planes does not appear to have been established in general. While Delaunay surfaces (unduloids/nodoids) provide the classical rotational examples, no published result is found establishing or refuting that every compact embedded CMC surface spanning such a boundary must be rotational.

status_evidence.title: Constant mean curvature surfaces (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: pieces of rotational (non spherical) cmc surfaces whose boundary is formed by two coaxial circles
status_evidence.claim: The configuration of CMC surfaces bounded by two coaxial circles is studied; rotational examples exist (Delaunay), but uniqueness in the embedded compact case is not asserted.

status_evidence.title: Constant-mean-curvature surface - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Delaunay (1841): the only surfaces of revolution with constant mean curvature are plane, cylinder, sphere, catenoid, unduloid, nodoid.
status_evidence.claim: Rotational CMC surfaces are completely classified, providing the candidate solutions, but the question of whether all compact embedded CMC surfaces spanning two coaxial circles must be rotational is not addressed.
